title: Pearl S. Buck: The First American Woman to Win a Nobel Prize in Literature

source.name: VOA Learning English — Pearl S. Buck: The First American Woman to Win a Nobel Prize in Literature
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: The year was 1931. The top selling book in the United States was The Good Earth by Pearl S. Buck.
The following year, Buck won the Pulitzer Prize for the best novel by an American writer.

In 1938, Buck became the first American woman to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She wrote more than one hundred books. She also wrote short stories, poetry, plays, essays, and children’s books. But most people remember Pearl Buck for her novels about China. She knew the country and its people very well. For nearly 40 years, China was her home.
Pearl’s parents were Caroline and Absalom Sydenstricker. They were religious workers in China.
Pearl’s education began at home. Her mother taught her many of the things she would have learned in an American school. A Chinese teacher taught Pearl other subjects.

In 1910, Pearl went back to the United States to study philosophy at Randolph-Macon Woman’s College in Lynchburg, Virginia. After graduation , she returned to China. Three years later, she met John Lossing Buck. He was a religious worker who studied agriculture. They were married and moved to a small village in the north of China. Their life among the poorest people provided the subject matter for many of the books she later wrote.
The Good Earth is the story of a poor Chinese man named Wang Lung. His wife is O-Lan. They work very hard together and finally make enough money to buy some land for a farm.
After a time, they grow enough crops to feed their family well, with some left over to sell. Their lives get much better, and they are happy. But the good times do not last.
Pearl Buck wrote her first books about China at a time when most people in the world knew almost nothing about the Chinese way of life.

After almost 40 years in China, the writer moved back to the United States. She bought Green Hills Farm in eastern Pennsylvania. She began to write articles for newspapers and magazines. She expressed her opinions on war, politics, religion, equal rights for all people and many other subjects.
She also gave many speeches. Buck talked to young people about the importance of a good education. She also told them they needed to know more about other people around the world.
Pearl Buck died in 1973 at the age of 80.

questions.q: Why is Pearl Buck remembered mainly for her novels about China?
options: She understood China well after living there for so long
She was born in China and never left the country again
She never wrote about any other subject during her career
The Chinese government had asked her to write them
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: dù viết hơn 100 cuốn thuộc nhiều thể loại, bà được nhớ nhờ tiểu thuyết về Trung Quốc vì “knew the country and its people very well”; Trung Quốc là nhà gần 40 năm.

questions.q: What can be understood about Pearl’s early schooling?
options: She went to an American school from the age of five
She was taught only by Chinese teachers in a village school
She had no lessons at all until she went to college in Virginia
Both her mother and a Chinese teacher gave her lessons
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: giáo dục bắt đầu ở nhà – mẹ dạy nhiều môn như ở trường Mỹ, một thầy giáo Trung Quốc dạy các môn khác.

questions.q: What influenced the subject matter of many of Buck’s later books?
options: Years spent with very poor villagers after she got married
Her work as a newspaper writer on a farm in Pennsylvania
Her travels with her parents as they worked for their church
Her studies of philosophy at a college in Virginia
questions.explain: Đoạn 6: sau khi cưới, họ sống ở một ngôi làng phía bắc Trung Quốc; “their life among the poorest people provided the subject matter for many of the books she later wrote”.

questions.q: Which statement best summarises the story of The Good Earth as it is described here?
options: A poor farming couple improve their lives, but their happiness does not last
A rich landowner loses his money and decides to move to America
Two brothers invent a new machine that helps them to plant crops
A young teacher struggles to open a school in a Chinese village
questions.explain: Đoạn 7–8: Wang Lung và O-Lan nghèo, làm việc chăm chỉ, mua đất, cuộc sống khá hơn và hạnh phúc, nhưng “the good times do not last”.

questions.q: Why were Buck’s first books about China important?
options: They were written in Chinese for the people of her village
Few readers abroad had any idea how Chinese people lived
They were the first novels from America to win a famous prize
They taught readers how to set up a farm in a foreign country
questions.explain: Đoạn 9: bà viết khi “most people in the world knew almost nothing about the Chinese way of life”.

questions.q: What message did Buck give to young people in her speeches?
options: Move to China to learn the skills needed for modern farming
Stay away from politics and concentrate only on your own country
Study hard and learn more about people in other countries
Read newspapers instead of novels so that you understand the world
questions.explain: Đoạn 11: bà nói về tầm quan trọng của giáo dục tốt và cần “know more about other people around the world”.

questions.q: Buck won a major American prize for fiction in the year after The Good Earth was the best-selling book in the country.
questions.explain: Đoạn 1–2: năm 1931 The Good Earth bán chạy nhất; “the following year” (1932) bà giành giải Pulitzer cho tiểu thuyết hay nhất.

questions.q: Buck’s husband encouraged her to begin writing novels.
questions.explain: Bài không nói ai động viên bà bắt đầu viết.
